Quarto is amazing, for reproducable reports, quick dashboards, websites and blogging sites like mine. Quarto has an extension ecosystem as well, so I started playing with these extensions, thus, this post will document some of example works around these extensions. 

## Share-post
This is an amazing extions that can add a social media post to your document. I wish they had named it Embed-post rather than share-post. Below is an example. 

My Linkedin post:
{{< share-post https://www.linkedin.com/feed/update/urn:li:activity:7335234505370169344 >}}

Below is the markdown of the above post (it does not appear till the time I add space between `{{` and `<`.)

```

{{ < share-post https://www.linkedin.com/feed/update/urn:li:activity:7335234505370169344 > }}

```

Ooops, markdown is not appearing, not sure why. 

I tried Twitter post, initially had some challages and still it is not working. 

{{< share-post https://x.com/mnabiahmad/status/1790665983985586553?s=20 >}}

Twitter post as markdown and it does not appear till the time I add space between `{{` and `<`.

```
{{ < share-post https://x.com/mnabiahmad/status/1790665983985586553 > }} 
```

Somehow the twitter post is not appearing, thus, I tired using twitter's embed option and it shows (see below).

## Quarto social share
[Quarto social share](https://github.com/schochastics/quarto-social-share) is an other amazing extension. I am using this extension in this post as well so you can check at the bottom. 

It is very easy to use and the offical [github repo ](https://github.com/schochastics/quarto-social-share) expians everything. 

## Quarto Badges
[Qyarto Badges](https://github.com/mcanouil/quarto-badge) are small visual improvement but looks cool and has option of becoming a link. 

First install the extions using `quarto add mcanouil/quarto-badge` command. Second, defind badge style either in the post under extension heading (see code section below) or in _quarto.yml file. 

```
.
.
extensions:
  badge:
    - key: current
      colour: springgreen
      href: https://github.com/mcanouil/quarto-badge/releases/tag/{{value}}

```

Some examples, current badge {{< badge current 1.0.0 >}}, future badge {{< badge future 2.0.0 >}}, old badge {{< badge old 0.1.0 >}}, hmm old page is not appearing .

## Lightbox
Allow photos to appear in separate popup (and a bit of zoom-in on photos), no need of installation as this extension is now part of deafult installation. You can read more about at [Light box repo](https://github.com/quarto-ext/lightbox)

An example below 

![Image using lightbox extension](quarto_extension1.png){.lightbox}

The best part is that it can be used with code block as well, see the code block below. Note you also need [R](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=REditorSupport.r) extension to run R code in VSCode. Of course, you need to install R on your machine + rmarkdown and languageserver package in R by using `install.packages("rmarkdown")`. 

```
#| fig-cap: Simple demo R plot 
#| lightbox:
#|   group: r-graph
#|   description: This is 1 to 10 plot
plot(1:10, rnorm(10))
```

```{r}
#| fig-cap: Simple demo R plot 
#| lightbox:
#|   group: r-graph
#|   description: This is 1 to 10 plot
plot(1:10, rnorm(10))
```


Python require jupyter extension (working)
```
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# 1. Prepare data (if only one list is provided, it is used for the y-axis, 
#    and the x-axis defaults to the index starting at 0)
y_values = [1, 4, 2, 3]

# 2. Create and customize the plot
plt.plot(y_values) # Plots the data on the Axes
plt.xlabel('X-axis Label') # Adds a label to the x-axis
plt.ylabel('Y-axis Label') # Adds a label to the y-axis
plt.title('My Simple Matplotlib Plot') # Adds a title
plt.grid(True) # Adds a grid for better visualization

# 3. Display the plot
plt.show() # Shows the figure window
```
